title: rorca-ultimate-ux
description: Principal-level UX overhaul: eliminate all panel redundancy (30 panels → 5 screens), Fizzy-inspired kanban with collapsible color-coded columns, unified spec lifecycle (Forge + Review + Archive = one flow), consolidated analytics (8 panels → 1), production-grade drag-and-drop, keyboard navigation, responsive design, and accessibility. Every story maps sysgazer skills for execution-time injection. This spec builds on the completed rorca-ux-overhaul (15 stories passed) and eliminates remaining UX debt.

userStories.title: Unified Spec Lifecycle Panel — Replace Forge + Queue + Archive
userStories.description:
As a user, I want ONE panel that shows my entire spec lifecycle (draft → in-progress → custom columns → done) — so I never have to jump between Forge, Wake/Queue, and Archive to manage specs.

This replaces three separate panels (SpecForgePanelPage, QueuePanel, ArchivePanel) with a single Specs panel that has two views: Board (Fizzy-inspired kanban) and List (searchable archive table). The Board view IS the kanban with system columns (Draft, In Progress, Done) plus custom columns. The List view IS the current Archive with search, tags, and telemetry. Toggle between views with a segmented control.

The spec generation form (brief input + model selector + advanced options) lives in a slide-over triggered by a '+ New Spec' button, not as a separate panel.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/panels/SpecsPanel.tsx replaces SpecForgePanelPage.tsx, QueuePanel.tsx, and ArchivePanel.tsx
Two-view toggle: 'Board' (kanban) and 'List' (archive table) — persisted in localStorage
Board view renders system columns (Draft, In Progress, Done) plus custom kanban_columns from DB
List view renders searchable/filterable/sortable table of ALL specs (pending + approved + archived) with status badges, tags, run telemetry, and pagination
'+  New Spec' button in top-right opens a slide-over with: brief textarea, model selector, direction preview, advanced options (stories count, parallelism, model override)
Spec cards in Board view are draggable between ALL columns (system + custom) using HTML5 DnD with proper visual feedback (ghost, drop zone highlight, column color tint)
Clicking a spec card in either view opens a spec detail slide-over (replaces SpecReviewPanel) with: stories list, approve/reject buttons, edit brief, version history, raw JSON
Archive search (full-text, tag filter, date range, status filter) works in List view

All existing QueuePanel kanban functionality preserved: custom columns, color picker, drag-and-drop, collapsible columns, inline rename
All existing ArchivePanel functionality preserved: search, tags, telemetry, fork, publish, export
All existing Forge functionality preserved: brief input, model selection, batch forge, spec generation progress

userStories.title: Fizzy-Inspired Collapsible Columns with Progress Indicators
userStories.description:
As a user managing many specs across columns, I want columns to collapse into slim vertical labels with card-count progress bars — so I can see all columns at a glance and expand only the ones I'm working with.

Inspired by Fizzy's collapsible column pattern: collapsed columns show a vertical rotated label, a count badge, and a color-gradient progress bar proportional to card count. Expanding a column on desktop doesn't collapse others (unlike Fizzy's mobile behavior). Columns animate smoothly with CSS transitions (300ms ease-out). Column state persists in localStorage per workspace.
acceptanceCriteria: Collapsed column width: 40px. Expanded column: flex 1 with min-width 280px
Collapsed state shows: vertical rotated column name (writing-mode: vertical-rl), card count badge, color gradient progress bar (height proportional to card count, max 50vh)
Click collapsed column header to expand, click expanded column header to collapse
CSS transition on width change: 300ms with ease-out-overshoot curve (cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1))
Column collapse state persisted in localStorage keyed by workspace ID + column ID
On initial load, restore collapsed state from localStorage; default all expanded
Progress bar gradient: from column color (top) to transparent (bottom), using CSS color-mix()
Responsive: on viewports < 640px, columns stack vertically and collapse is disabled (all expanded, scroll horizontally with snap)
Keyboard: Enter/Space toggles collapse on focused column header
Column header shows: color dot + column name + card count + collapse/expand chevron icon

userStories.title: Production Drag-and-Drop with Keyboard Accessibility
userStories.description:
As a user, I want drag-and-drop that actually works reliably — no lag, no missed drops, no button-swallowing events — plus keyboard-only card movement for accessibility.

Replace the current HTML5 DnD implementation with a robust system: cards use div[role=button][draggable] (never nested button elements), drag ghost shows card title with column color tint, drop zones highlight with dashed border and background color, drag-leave debounced at 50ms to prevent flicker between child elements. Add keyboard card movement: focus card → arrow keys to move between columns, Enter to confirm drop.
acceptanceCriteria: All spec cards use <div role='button' tabIndex={0} draggable> — no nested <button> elements that swallow drag events
On dragstart: set draggingSpecId state, apply 0.5 opacity to source card, dataTransfer carries JSON { specId, fromColumnId, fromColumnType }
On dragover: highlight target column with dashed 2px border in column color + 15% opacity background fill. Debounce dragLeave by 50ms to prevent flicker
On drop: execute correct backend action based on source→target transition (approve, unapprove, assign, unassign, reassign) with optimistic UI update + rollback on error

Drop transitions: draft→approved (POST approve), approved→draft (POST unapprove), approved→custom (POST assign), custom→custom (POST assign), custom→approved (DELETE assignment), any→done is blocked (done is read-only from pipeline completion)
Keyboard movement: Tab to focus card → Ctrl+Arrow Left/Right to move card to adjacent column → screen reader announcement of new column name
Drag ghost (dataTransfer.setDragImage): custom rendered element showing card title + column color stripe, positioned 10px offset from cursor
Touch support: onTouchStart/onTouchMove/onTouchEnd handlers that simulate drag behavior on mobile (long-press 300ms to initiate)
aria-live region announces: 'Moved [spec title] from [source column] to [target column]' after each successful move
Performance: no re-renders during drag (use refs for drag state, not useState). Board stays at 60fps during drag operations
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Custom Column Management — Add, Rename, Reorder, Delete with Color Picker

userStories.title: Spec Card Redesign — Rich Information Density
userStories.description:
As a user scanning the kanban board, I want spec cards that show key information at a glance — title, story count, status progress, model used, last activity, assigned tags — without clicking into each card.

Redesign the KanbanSpecCard component with richer information density inspired by Fizzy's card design: title as primary text, story progress bar (passed/failed/pending as green/red/grey segments), model badge, time-ago stamp, tag pills (max 2 visible + overflow count), subtle color tint from column color. Cards should feel tactile — slight shadow on hover, scale(1.02) lift on drag.

Model badge: small pill showing model name (e.g., 'opus-4-6', 'gpt-4o') with provider color (purple=Anthropic, green=OpenAI, blue=Google)
Time-ago: relative time since last activity (e.g., '2h ago', '3d ago') using lightweight formatter, not moment.js
Tag pills: show first 2 tags as colored pills, +N overflow badge if more. Click overflow to see all tags in a popover
Column color tint: card left border (3px) in column color. On hover: full card background shifts to 5% opacity column color
Drag feedback: on dragstart, card gets opacity 0.5 + scale(0.98). Hovering over a valid drop column: card ghost shows scale(1.02) + shadow-lg

Sidebar: bottom tab bar on mobile (5 icons), collapsible rail on tablet, full sidebar on desktop. Slide-overs: full-screen on mobile, 480px on desktop.

userStories.title: Dark Mode Polish and Theme Consistency
userStories.description:
As a user who prefers dark mode, I want consistent dark theme across ALL panels — no white flashes, no mismatched backgrounds, no unreadable text on dark surfaces.

Audit every panel and component for dark mode consistency. Fix: all backgrounds use CSS custom properties (not hardcoded colors), all text colors have dark variants, charts use dark-friendly color palette, borders use subtle contrast (not invisible or too bright). Respect system preference (prefers-color-scheme) with manual override in Settings.
acceptanceCriteria: All hardcoded color values (bg-white, text-gray-900, border-gray-200, etc.) replaced with Tailwind dark: variants or CSS custom properties
Card backgrounds: bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900. Card borders: border-neutral-200 dark:border-neutral-700
Column backgrounds: color-mix(in srgb, var(--card-color) 15%, var(--color-canvas)) where --color-canvas is white/neutral-950 per theme
Charts: use palette that works on both light and dark backgrounds. No pure white or pure black in chart colors
Slide-over backdrop: bg-black/50 in light mode, bg-black/70 in dark mode
Input fields: consistent styling in dark mode — visible borders, readable placeholder text, proper focus ring color
Scrollbar styling: dark scrollbar track in dark mode (webkit-scrollbar-track: neutral-900)
Theme toggle in Settings > Account: System (default), Light, Dark. Persisted in localStorage + user_settings DB
No white flash on page load in dark mode: html element gets dark class before first paint (inline script in index.html)
All skeleton screens use dark-appropriate shimmer colors
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Toast and Notification Consistency
userStories.description:
As a user performing actions (approve, reject, run, save), I want consistent feedback — success toasts for happy paths, error toasts with actionable messages for failures, and a notification center for async events (run completed, spec generated).

Audit all user actions across all panels for consistent toast/notification behavior. Create a unified toast system with 4 types: success (green, auto-dismiss 3s), error (red, persistent until dismissed, shows retry action if applicable), warning (amber, auto-dismiss 5s), info (blue, auto-dismiss 3s). Notification center in sidebar for async events.
acceptanceCriteria: Toast component: positioned top-right, max 3 visible at once, newest on top. Stacks vertically with 8px gap

Toast types: success (green-500 accent, check icon, 3s auto-dismiss), error (red-500 accent, x-circle icon, persistent, shows action button if retryable), warning (amber-500 accent, alert-triangle icon, 5s auto-dismiss), info (blue-500 accent, info icon, 3s auto-dismiss)
Toast animations: slide in from right (200ms), slide out to right on dismiss (150ms)
All spec actions have toasts: approve ('Spec approved'), reject ('Spec rejected'), generate ('Spec generation started'), delete ('Spec deleted')
All run actions have toasts: trigger ('Pipeline started'), cancel ('Run cancelled'), pause ('Run paused'), resume ('Run resumed')
All settings saves have toasts: success ('Settings saved'), error ('Failed to save: [error message]')
Error toasts include: error message (from API response), retry button (if action is retryable), 'Copy error' button for debugging
Notification bell icon in sidebar header: shows unread count badge, click opens notification dropdown with recent async events (run completed, spec generated, health alert)
Notifications stored in notification_history DB table, fetched via GET /api/notifications
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Performance Optimization — Lazy Loading, Virtualization, Bundle Splitting
userStories.description:
As a user with many specs and long run histories, I want the app to stay fast — panels load instantly, long lists don't lag, and initial bundle is small.

Implement: React.lazy for all panel components (code-split per panel), virtual scrolling for lists > 50 items (react-window), intersection observer for lazy-loading card details in board view, debounced search inputs (300ms), and memoized expensive computations (useMemo for filtered/sorted lists). Target: < 200ms panel switch, < 100ms search response, < 2MB initial bundle.
acceptanceCriteria: All panel components loaded via React.lazy with Suspense fallback (skeleton screens from ULT-017)
Board view: cards outside viewport not rendered (intersection observer), rendered on scroll into view. 60fps scroll on boards with 100+ cards
List view: react-window VirtualList for spec archive (only renders visible rows + 5 overscan). Handles 10,000+ specs without lag
Search inputs (spec search, command palette, marketplace) debounced at 300ms using useDeferredValue or custom debounce hook
Expensive list operations (filter, sort, group by column) wrapped in useMemo with stable dependency arrays
API responses for lists include pagination: page, pageSize, total. Default pageSize=50. Infinite scroll fetches next page at 80% scroll position
Image/avatar loading: lazy loading with loading='lazy' attribute, placeholder blur-up
Bundle analysis: run npx vite-bundle-visualizer, ensure no single chunk > 500KB, total initial load < 2MB
No unnecessary re-renders: React DevTools Profiler shows < 5 renders per user interaction. Key components wrapped in React.memo where appropriate
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Accessibility Audit and WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance
userStories.description:
As a user with a disability, I want the app to be fully accessible — screen reader compatible, keyboard navigable, color-contrast compliant, and motion-reduced when requested.

Run a full accessibility audit against WCAG 2.1 AA criteria. Fix: all images have alt text, all interactive elements have accessible names, all color combinations meet 4.5:1 contrast ratio, all animations respect prefers-reduced-motion, all form fields have labels, all modals trap focus, all dynamic content updates announced via aria-live regions.
acceptanceCriteria: All interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs) have accessible names via aria-label, aria-labelledby, or visible text content
All images and icons have alt text or aria-hidden='true' (decorative icons)
Color contrast: all text/background combinations meet 4.5:1 ratio for normal text, 3:1 for large text. Verify with axe-core or Lighthouse
Keyboard navigation: every interactive element reachable via Tab, every action triggerable via Enter/Space, every modal closeable via Escape
Focus management: when slide-over opens, focus moves to first interactive element inside. When it closes, focus returns to trigger element
Screen reader: aria-live='polite' regions for: toast notifications, spec card moved (drag-and-drop), story status updates (SSE), search result counts
prefers-reduced-motion: all CSS animations and transitions disabled when user prefers reduced motion. JS animations (drag ghost, toast slide) also respect this
Form accessibility: all inputs have associated <label> elements (not just placeholder text), required fields marked with aria-required='true', validation errors linked via aria-describedby
Heading hierarchy: each panel has h1 (panel title), sections use h2, sub-sections use h3. No skipped heading levels
Landmark regions: <main> for panel content, <nav> for sidebar, <aside> for slide-overs, <header> for panel headers
Run axe-core automated tests: zero critical/serious violations. Add axe-core to Vitest setup for regression prevention
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Cleanup — Delete Redundant Panel Files and Update Routing
userStories.description:
As a developer maintaining Rorca, I want zero dead code — all deleted/consolidated panels removed from the codebase, routing updated, imports cleaned up.

Delete all panel files that were consolidated in previous stories. Update App.tsx routing, Sidebar.tsx navigation, and all cross-references. Verify no broken imports, no dead routes, no orphaned components.
acceptanceCriteria: Deleted files (consolidated into other panels): SpecReviewPanel.tsx (→ SpecDetailSlideOver), ActivityFeedPanel.tsx (→ Settings.System), AuditLogPanel.tsx (→ Settings.System), GitHubSettingsPanel.tsx (→ Settings.Integrations), WorktreesPanel.tsx (→ RunView tab), MemoryPanel.tsx (→ Direction tab), TeamDirectionPanel.tsx (→ Direction tab)

Deleted files (consolidated into AnalyticsPanel): UsageDashboardPanel.tsx, CostBreakdownPanel.tsx, ModelComparisonPanel.tsx, VelocityChartPanel.tsx, CompletionRatePanel.tsx, RoiCalculatorPanel.tsx, FinOpsDashboardPanel.tsx, HealthDashboardPanel.tsx
Deleted files (consolidated into SpecsPanel): SpecForgePanelPage.tsx, QueuePanel.tsx, ArchivePanel.tsx, TemplateMarketplacePanel.tsx (content moved, not just deleted)
App.tsx routes updated: /specs, /runs, /run-view/:id, /analytics, /direction, /settings/*
Old routes redirect to new: /forge→/specs, /queue→/specs?view=board, /archive→/specs?view=list, /pipeline→/runs, /marketplace→/specs?view=marketplace
PanelId type updated in Sidebar.tsx — old IDs removed, new IDs only
No TypeScript errors: npx tsc --noEmit passes for frontend
No broken imports: grep for deleted file names returns zero results in src/
No orphaned components: every component in src/components/ is imported somewhere
HubPanel.tsx deleted — its content distributed to Runs (active run card) and Specs (pending specs badge)
